original_question: Is it consistent that the independence number i is at most the ultrafilter number u and still \( inom{i}{\omega} 	o  inom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.11: the open problem stated as “Is it consistent that i ≤ u and \(\binom{i}{\omega} \to \binom{i}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?”
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended target essentially exactly: it asks a consistency question, uses the same two cardinal invariants (the independence number i and the ultrafilter number u), and states the same strong polarized partition relation at the pair \((i,\omega)\). This is the precise problem asked in Section 3, Problem 3.11.
missing_details: It should explicitly say that this is a consistency question over ZFC, i.e. whether there exists a model of set theory satisfying the stated conjunction.

It should unpack the arrow notation using Definition 1.1: \(\binom{\lambda}{\kappa} \to \binom{\lambda}{\kappa}^{1,1}_2\) means that for every coloring \(c:\lambda\times\kappa\to 2\), there are \(A\subseteq\lambda\) and \(B\subseteq\kappa\) with \(|A|=\lambda\) and \(|B|=\kappa\) such that \(c\) is constant on \(A\times B\).
To be stand-alone, it should identify i and u as the standard cardinal invariants of the continuum: the independence number and the ultrafilter number.
It should make explicit that the '2' in the subscript denotes a two-coloring and that the superscript \(^{1,1}\) refers to a monochromatic rectangle with full-sized components.
The paper places this in Section 3, which is specifically about polarized partition relations at the first infinite cardinal; so the small component is \(\omega\), not an arbitrary \(\kappa\).
refined_question: Is there a model of ZFC in which the independence number \(\mathfrak{i}\) is at most the ultrafilter number \(\mathfrak{u}\), and the strong polarized partition relation \(\binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega} \to \binom{\mathfrak{i}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\) holds; that is, for every coloring \(c:\mathfrak{i}\times\omega\to 2\), there exist \(A\subseteq\mathfrak{i}\) and \(B\subseteq\omega\) with \(|A|=\mathfrak{i}\) and \(|B|=\omega\) such that \(c\) is constant on \(A\times B\)?
justification: The draft is already almost verbatim the paper's official formulation. In Section 3, after Problem 3.10 on \(i=\aleph_1\), the authors state exactly the ultrafilter-number variant as Problem 3.11. Definition 1.1 supplies the missing meaning of the partition symbol, so the only real refinement needed is to make the consistency quantifier and the strong polarized relation fully explicit. The nearby context shows that this belongs to the paper's list of open problems about cardinal invariants at \(\omega\), not to the singular-cardinal results from the introduction; the authors also note that a forcing construction establishing the consistency of \(i<u\) may be relevant.
